fields.quoted_span: To calculate the dollar amount of the 1.6% annual rent increase, multiply the tenant's base rent by .016. For example, if the tenant's base rent is $2,000.00, the annual increase would be calculated as follows: $2,000.00 x .016 = $32.00.
fields.note: The 1.6% rate for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027, the calculation, the worked example and the prior 1.4% rate are supported. The 1.7% rate for 2024-25, the Certificate of Occupancy and Costa-Hawkins exemptions, and the just-cause eviction statement do not appear in this document. The document does not say the rate is reset each March 1.

fields.quoted_span: the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
fields.note: The 1.6% rate, the base rent x .016 method and the prior 1.4% (2025-26) are supported. The 1.7% (2024-25) figure is not in this document.

fields.quoted_span: the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
fields.note: The March 1, 2026 start of the rate period is stated.

fields.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
fields.note: The document is a January 14, 2026 announcement of a rate that takes effect March 1, 2026. It does not explicitly state the legal status of the rule, but in-force status is consistent with it.

fields.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
fields.note: The document supports only that the rate applies to rent-controlled units. The June 13, 1979 Certificate of Occupancy cutoff, the Costa-Hawkins exemption, the exemption for rents regulated by another agency and the eviction-provision carve-out are not in this document.
